reconcile.note: John Gill reads the figures as sequential eras: patriarchs living centuries before the flood, a post-flood cap near a hundred twenty years, then Moses's seventy as his era's norm.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues the numbers at face value, noting that Noah and several other post-flood patriarchs lived far beyond the hundred-twenty-year limit Genesis attributes to God.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "What is the human life span?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/lifespan.html).

sides.snippet: yet will his days be one hundred twenty years.
sides.verseText: Yahweh said, \"My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; yet will his days be one hundred twenty years.\"

sides.snippet: All the days of Noah were nine hundred fifty years, then he died.
sides.verseText: All the days of Noah were nine hundred fifty years, then he died.
